title: Weather, seasons, and comparing
goal: Talking about the weather and the seasons, then comparing two things — with a single preposition that replaces the whole English "more ... than".
bekal: describe the weather and Afghanistan's four seasons
compare two things with تر ... ښه

dialogs.title: خبرې اترې — د ژمي لومړۍ ورځ
dialogs.intro: A December morning. The first snow fell overnight and all of Kabul has changed color. Budi stands at the window with a steaming cup of tea.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.id: Snow! The whole city is white.

lines.speaker: نجیب:
lines.text: هو، د ژمي لومړۍ واوره ده. نن ډېره یخني ده.
lines.baca: ho, də zhamī lūmṛəy wāwra da. nən ḍera yakhnī da.
lines.id: Yes, the first snow of winter. It's very cold today.
lines.literal: yes, of winter first snow is. today very cold is.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: کابل تر جاکارتا ډېر یخ دی.
lines.baca: Kābəl tər Jākārtā ḍer yakh day.
lines.id: Kabul is much colder than Jakarta.
lines.literal: Kabul from Jakarta much cold is.

lines.speaker: نجیب:
lines.text: هرومرو. جاکارتا کې واوره نه ورېږي، سمه ده؟
lines.baca: harūmarū. Jākārtā ke wāwra nə wrīẓī, sama da?
lines.id: Of course. It doesn't snow in Jakarta, right?
lines.literal: of-course. Jakarta in snow not falls-it, right is?

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: هېڅکله. زمونږ دوه موسمه دي — باران او ګرمي.
lines.baca: hetskəla. zmūẓ dwa mosama dī — bārān aw garmī.
lines.id: Never. We have two seasons — rainy and hot.
lines.literal: never. of-ours two seasons are — rain and heat.

lines.speaker: نجیب:
lines.text: زمونږ څلور دي. خو ژمی تر ټولو اوږد دی.
lines.baca: zmūẓ tsalor dī. kho zhamay tər ṭolo ūẓd day.
lines.id: We have four. But winter is the longest.
lines.literal: of-ours four are. but winter from all long is.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: کوم موسم تر ټولو ښکلی دی؟
lines.baca: kūm mosam tər ṭolo ṣkulay day?
lines.id: Which season is the most beautiful?
lines.literal: which season from all beautiful is?

lines.speaker: نجیب:
lines.text: پسرلی. هر څه شین کېږي او نوروز راځي.
lines.baca: psarlay. har tsə shīn keẓī aw Nawroz rādzī.
lines.id: Spring. Everything turns green and Nowruz comes.
lines.literal: spring. every thing green becomes and Nowruz comes-it.

lines.speaker: نجیب:
lines.text: زمونږ نوی کال. د پسرلي لومړۍ ورځ، د مارچ په یویشتمه.
lines.baca: zmūẓ naway kāl. də psarlī lūmṛəy wradz, də mārch pə yawwishtama.
lines.id: Our New Year. The first day of spring, the twenty-first of March.
lines.literal: of-ours new year. of spring first day, of March on twenty-one.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.id: And summer? Is it very hot?

lines.speaker: نجیب:
lines.text: په کابل کې نه. خو جلال آباد تر کابل ډېر ګرم وي.
lines.baca: pə Kābəl ke nə. kho Jalālābād tər Kābəl ḍer garm wī.
lines.id: Not in Kabul. But Jalalabad is much hotter than Kabul.
lines.literal: in Kabul in no. but Jalalabad from Kabul much hot usually-is.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: نو ژمي کې خلک جلال آباد ته ځي؟
lines.baca: no zhamī ke khalk Jalālābād ta dzī?
lines.id: So in winter people go to Jalalabad?
lines.literal: so winter in people Jalalabad to go-they?

lines.speaker: نجیب:
lines.text: هو، دقیقاً. دوه ساعته لار ده، خو بل موسم دی.
lines.baca: ho, daqīqan. dwa sā'ata lār da, kho bəl mosam day.
lines.id: Yes, exactly. Two hours' drive, but a different season.
lines.literal: yes, exactly. two hours road is, but other season is.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: دا زما لپاره عجیبه ده. زمونږ هر ځای یو شان دی.
lines.baca: dā zmā ləpāra ajība da. zmūẓ har dzāy yaw shān day.
lines.id: That's strange to me. Back home everywhere is the same.
lines.literal: this of-mine for strange is. of-ours every place one kind is.

notes: Comparing in Pashto needs neither "more" nor "than". All it uses is one preposition: **تر**. کابل **تر** جاکارتا یخ دی is literally "Kabul from Jakarta cold is", and it means "Kabul is colder than Jakarta".
⚠️ The adjective **doesn't change form** when comparing. English turns *cold* into *colder*; Pashto leaves یخ as یخ. Only تر marks the comparison, and nothing is added to the adjective.
To say "the most", use **تر ټولو**, literally "from all". ژمی **تر ټولو** اوږد دی means "winter is the longest". Once again, the adjective stays plain.
The word ډېر before an adjective means "much more" in a comparison, and "very" in an ordinary sentence. کابل تر جاکارتا **ډېر** یخ دی means "Kabul is much colder", not "Kabul is very cold".

The word **نوروز** is the solar New Year, celebrated in Afghanistan, Iran, Central Asia, and Kurdistan on the first day of spring. Afghanistan's biggest celebration is in Mazar-e Sharif, and hundreds of thousands of people come. It's not a religious holiday but a seasonal one.
Note once more the وي in کوم موسم ډېر ګرم **وي**. Because seasonal weather is a habit repeated every year, Pashto uses وي, not دی. This is the use of وي you'll meet most often.

grammars.title: Comparing with تر
body: The order is: first thing, **تر**, second thing, plain adjective, then the verb "to be". What's being compared stands before تر; what it's compared with comes after.
To strengthen it, add **ډېر** before the adjective. To soften it, add **لږ**: کابل تر هرات **لږ** یخ دی means "Kabul is a little colder than Herat".

grammars.title: Weather: sentences without a clear subject
body: Pashto doesn't use a dummy subject like English "it". Weather sentences use **هوا** (air) as the subject, or just use the verb itself: باران ورېږي (rain is falling).
Note that هوا is feminine, so the sentence is هوا ښه **ده**, not ښه دی. This is one of the words beginners get wrong most often, because it doesn't end in ه.

sections.title: Four seasons, and the language to describe them

head: Pashto
Say it
Season
In Afghanistan
rows: March to May. Nowruz, almond blossom, full rivers.
June to August. Kabul warm, Jalalabad very hot.
September to November. Grape and pomegranate harvest.
December to February. Snow in Kabul, mountain roads closed.

blocks.title: ⚠️ One word for green and blue: شین
items: The word **شین** *shīn* means green **and** blue at once. Grass is شین, the sky is شین too, and speakers don't feel anything is missing.
When the difference matters, a description is added: **د آسمان رنګ** (sky color) for blue, and **د بوټو رنګ** (plant color) for green. The loanword **آبي** *ābī* is also used for blue in cities.

English keeps the two apart, so this is one place where you have to **let go** of a precision you already have, rather than learn a new one. Green tea is شین چای, and nobody will mistake it for blue tea.
The same happens with **تور**, which means both black and dark, and with **سپین**, which means both white and light.

blocks.title: Nowruz, and why it isn't Eid
items: Nowruz falls on the first day of spring, around **March 21**, and marks the New Year of the solar calendar officially used in Afghanistan.
The biggest celebration is in **مزار شریف**, where a great banner is raised at the blue shrine and hundreds of thousands gather for forty days.
Its special dish is **هفت مېوه** *haft mewa* — seven kinds of dried fruit and nuts soaked in water overnight: raisins, apricots, almonds, pistachios, walnuts, and two more.
⚠️ Nowruz is not a religious holiday and doesn't replace Eid al-Fitr (**کوچنی اختر**) or Eid al-Adha (**لوی اختر**). All three are celebrated, and all three are completely different.
This book is better than that one.

پسرلی — اوړی — منی — ژمی — کوم موسم تر ټولو ښکلی دی؟
کابل تر جاکارتا یخ دی. — ژمی تر ټولو اوږد دی. — نن باران ورېږي. — هوا ښه ده. — دواړه یو شان دي.
wave: Compare five pairs of things around you today with تر, without changing the adjective at all. If your hand wants to add something to the end of the adjective, hold back — that's your English habit still talking.
